text:
Ava (Mktg): Quick ask — launching a short webinar on inference economics next Wed. Need a small visual kit: 3 hero frames (social / slide hero / email header), 2 sequence diagrams showing 'request -> routing -> fallback', and a compact 1‑page cheat-sheet for SDRs. Deadline: Tue EOD for first pass.

Jamal (Design): Got it. Can you drop the content bullets and any benchmark numbers? also FYI — I only have bandwidth tomorrow morning. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Priya (Product Marketing): I'll paste the narrative bullets below. Keep copy tight — legal needs to sign off on one line about customer data.

Priya (Product Marketing): • Claim: "Predictable inference economics: latency you can budget for"
• Supporting stat: "~2.3x cost reduction vs naive serving with batching + KV cache (internal benchmark)"
• CTA for slides/email: "See configuration guide + live demo"
• SDR cheat-sheet bullets: top 3 talking points, one-liner about routing/fallback, link to demo sign-up

Ava (Mktg): Figma file: https://figma.com/redwood/inference-launch-kit (view only). For hero frames use 1200x628 and 800x800 variants. For slide hero use 1920x1080.

Jamal (Design): Cool. Two quick Qs: (1) visual style for sequence diagrams — linear swimlane or stacked cards? (2) do we need annotated tooltips for the sparkline cost chart?

Eli (Webinar PM): Swimlane is easier to animate in keynote. Tooltips: yes, we want hover/callout text for 3 data points: baseline, batched+cache, dedicated. Also we need a short 20s animated slide showing graceful fallback to cheaper model.

Jamal (Design): Sounds good. I'll mock swimlane + a compact sparkline with callouts. Will include a static annotated PNG + motion spec.

Sasha (Legal): Quick flag: avoid comparative language like "2.3x cheaper than X" unless we specify methodology. The wording "cost reduction vs naive serving with batching + KV cache (internal benchmark)" is OK if we add "internal test workload; results may vary" as fine print. I can sign off if fine print included.

Priya (Product Marketing): Aye — add the fine print. Also include a link to the benchmark appendix if people want details.

Jamal (Design): Plan: initial mockups by Tue 11am (PNG placeholders), animated slide prototype by Tue 5pm. Will push frames to the Figma file and tag @Ava @Eli. If anyone wants to jump in for copy tweaks ping me.

DesignBot: New comment on file  /inference-launch-kit/frame-3: "sparkline tooltip copy needed"

Ava (Mktg): I'll draft tooltip copy now. Short ones:
- Baseline: "single-request, no batching — higher unit cost"
- Batched + cache: "workload-aware batching + KV cache — lower cost, similar latency"
- Dedicated: "reserved capacity — predictable latency and throughput"

Jamal (Design): Perfect. Sasha, can you confirm the fine print phrasing?

Sasha (Legal): Confirmed: please add the footnote exactly: "Internal benchmark on representative test workload; actual results vary by model and traffic patterns." Approve once that's added. :white_check_mark:

Eli (Webinar PM): For SDR cheat-sheet, here's a short routing spiel: "We route by policy (latency-first, cost-first, region) and automatically fallback to compatible variants to preserve availability." Keep to one sentence.

Ava (Mktg): Great. Owners: Jamal (visuals), Priya (copy + cheat-sheet), Sasha (legal sign-off). If Jamal can upload first-pass assets by Tue 11am we'll run a quick review Wed morning. :rocket:

Priya (Product Marketing): I'll add copy to Figma comments and attach the cheat-sheet doc.

Jamal (Design): Tagged the assets and added a short motion spec. Will DM anyone who wants to jump on quick review slot Tue 11:30.

Ava (Mktg): Thanks team!
